source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Review the brand name and purchase cost, then rely on the pharmacy label for the remaining instructions.","B":"Review the medication's purpose, dose and schedule, important side effects and precautions, relevant interactions, and what to do if a dose is missed.","C":"Review only the dose and administration time because discussing expected effects or adverse effects can reduce adherence.","D":"Review the tablet's appearance and storage but omit missed-dose instructions because the response is the same for all medicines."}}
source_row.rationale: Safe medication self-management teaching includes why the medicine is used, dose and schedule, expected effects, important adverse effects and precautions, relevant interactions, and medication-specific instructions for missed doses. Option B is the only complete teaching plan. The other choices omit essential safety information or incorrectly imply that missed-dose instructions are universal.
source_row.source_detail: FDA — Think It Through: Managing the Benefits and Risks of Medicines, ‘Know Your Medicines’: know what each medicine is for, when and how to take it, what to do for a missed dose, expected effects, important side effects/precautions, and relevant interactions. Current FDA medication-safety consumer guidance at cited URL; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, calculations, adverse effects/interactions, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
